newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to seek to extend Palestinian aid law.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to seek to extend Palestinian aid law.

text.p: The U.S. State Department said on Monday it would work with Congress to try to extend, at least temporarily, a law that expires next month that makes possible U.S. aid to the Palestinians.

Expiration of the Middle East Peace Facilitation Act (MEPFA) would cut off U.S. financial assistance to the Palestinians, end diplomatic contacts and force the Palestine Liberation Organisation to close its Washington office.
The law expires Aug. 12, but Congress leaves for its August recess at the end of this week.
"We're going to be working with Congress now on seeing if we can find ways to achieve at least a temporary extension of MEPFA," said State Department deputy spokesman James Foley.

Anti-Palestinian sentiment has been rising in Congress over the past six months as negotiations between Israel and the Palestinians over implementing their agreement have broken down and violence has flared in the occupied territories.

Among other things, the U.S. law requires the administration to certify that the Palestinians are meeting their commitments under 1993 and 1995 peace agreements with Israel that provide for Palestinian self-rule in the West Bank and Gaza.

Foley said the certification of compliance was "something we are looking at." He said a particular focus was security cooperation with Israel, which the Palestinians withdrew in March in a dispute over Israeli settlement policy.
"I can't speculate on how this will come out. We have to prepare a report, we have to compile the facts, and that's what we're doing," he told reporters.

Earlier, State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters travelling with Secretary of State Madeleine Albright in Malaysia that aid to the Palestinians had been the basis of U.S. policy since 1993 and should continue.

The United States has provided $260 million out of a five-year commitment of $500 million to the Palestinians and "we think in the interest of peace we need to continue assistance to the Palestinian people," Burns said.
Burns stressed that most if not all of the U.S. funds go to non-governmental organisations that work with the Palestinian people, not to the Palestinian Authority.
Ending aid to the Palestinians would be another major blow to the struggling Middle East peace process.

High-level peace talks stopped in March, but Israel and the PLO agreed on Monday that joint committees would renew talks on outstanding issues such as the opening of Gaza air and sea ports and safe passage between the West Bank and Gaza.
